title: Geometric Superconducting Diode Effect in an NbN Nanoring
summary: Superconducting diodes, which exhibit nonreciprocal critical currents, are promising building blocks for low-power cryogenic electronics and superconducting circuits. Existing superconducting diode platforms commonly rely on Josephson junctions, multilayer heterostructures, ferromagnetic elements, gate-difined structures. Here, we demonstrate a geometrically induced superconducting diode effect realized in a structurally minimal, single-materials NbN nanoring, where inversion-symmetry breaking is introduced solely by the asymmetric geometry. The device exhibits pronounced and polarity-switchable critical-current nonreciprocity. Systematic magnetic-field and temperature-dependent measurements reveal that, at low fields, the applied magnetic field redistributes the critical current asymmetrically between opposite bias directions without significantly reducing the overall superconducting current-carrying capability. Moreover, the maximal nonreciprocity and diode efficiency exhibit distinct temperature dependence: the maximal diode efficiency follows the evolution of the energy gap, whereas the maximal nonreciprocity is more closely associated with the superfluid density. These results establish asymmetric superconducting nanorings as a minimal geometric platform for studying nonreciprocal superconducting transport and provide a simple design principle for future superconducting electronics.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates a geometrically induced superconducting diode effect in a single-material NbN nanoring, where asymmetric geometry alone breaks inversion symmetry, producing polarity-switchable nonreciprocal critical currents. The maximal diode efficiency follows the energy gap, while maximal nonreciprocity correlates with superfluid density.
AI.motivation: To realize a superconducting diode effect using a structurally minimal, single-material platform without Josephson junctions, multilayer heterostructures, ferromagnetic elements, or gate-defined structures.
AI.method: A geometrically asymmetric NbN nanoring is fabricated from a single material, where inversion-symmetry breaking is introduced solely by the asymmetric geometry. Systematic magnetic-field and temperature-dependent measurements are performed to characterize the diode effect.
AI.result: The device exhibits pronounced and polarity-switchable critical-current nonreciprocity. At low fields, the applied magnetic field redistributes the critical current asymmetrically between opposite bias directions without significantly reducing overall superconducting current-carrying capability. Maximal diode efficiency follows the energy gap evolution, while maximal nonreciprocity correlates with superfluid density.
AI.conclusion: Asymmetric superconducting nanorings serve as a minimal geometric platform for studying nonreciprocal superconducting transport, offering a simple design principle for future superconducting electronics.

title: Evidence for fully-gapped superconductivity in BCS superconductor NiBi3
summary: We investigate the physical characteristics, normal state and superconducting properties of NiBi3 single crystals. Measurements of electrical resistivity, magnetization, and London penetration depth demonstrate a superconducting transition temperature, Tc=4.0 K, with a sharp transition in resistivity (Tc = 0.20 K) and RRR = 18, reflecting the high quality of NiBi3 single crystals. With both orientations H perpendicular b and H parallel b of NiBi3 single crystals, we estimated the upper critical field, Hc2, from the magnetization data. In both orientations, Hc2 is significantly smaller than the Pauli limit, suggesting the orbital pair breaking in superconducting state. The coherence length, xi(0) = 26.78 nm, electron-phonon coupling constant, lambda(e-p) = 0.81, and penetration depth, lambda0 = 181.8 nm, suggest type-II superconductivity in NiBi3. In the superconducting state, lambda(T) is best described by an s-wave BCS model and does not have linear or quadratic dependency with T, which is in line with the expectation for a node-less superconducting order parameter. The temperature evolution of the superfluid density, obtained from lambda(T), reveals a fully gapped superconductivity in NiBi3, with a superconducting gap = 4.07. All the results from the present study indicate that NiBi3 is a typical type-II, BCS-like, moderately strong coupled, and fully gapped superconductor in the dirty limit.

AI.tldr: NiBi3 single crystals are characterized as type-II, BCS-like, moderately strong-coupled, fully gapped superconductors with Tc=4.0 K, dirty limit behavior, and s-wave pairing symmetry.
AI.motivation: To investigate the physical characteristics, normal state, and superconducting properties of high-quality NiBi3 single crystals, and determine the nature of their superconductivity.
AI.method: Measurements of electrical resistivity, magnetization, and London penetration depth on NiBi3 single crystals with orientations H ⟂ b and H ∥ b, analyzed via BCS s-wave model.
AI.result: Tc=4.0 K, ΔTc=0.20 K, RRR=18; upper critical field Hc2 below Pauli limit; coherence length ξ(0)=26.78 nm, λ₀=181.8 nm, λₑ₋ₚ=0.81; fully gapped s-wave superconductivity with gap Δ=4.07; dirty limit type-II behavior.
AI.conclusion: NiBi3 is a typical type-II, BCS-like, moderately strong-coupled, fully gapped superconductor in the dirty limit, consistent with a node-less superconducting order parameter.

title: Magnetically memorable inductance in superconducting multilayer resonators
summary: Superconductor-ferromagnet hybrid structures with tunable kinetic inductance are promising elements for neuromorphic and quantum computing circuits. We report the fabrication and microwave characterization of split-ring resonators based on Nb/Co/Nb/Co/Nb/Al spin-trigger multilayers and demonstrate a non-volatile spin-valve effect on their resonant properties. Reversal of the relative magnetization orientation of the cobalt layers produces a reproducible shift of the resonant frequency up to 4 MHz at zero applied magnetic field, corresponding to a change in the kinetic inductance of the structure. The incorporation of a proximitized aluminum overlayer is shown to enhance the inductance contrast between the parallel and antiparallel magnetic states by a factor of approximately three relative to structures without this layer. The experimental results are in quantitative agreement with a microscopic model based on the Usadel equations. The demonstrated magnetic memory of the resonant frequency at zero field establishes spin-trigger multilayers as viable field-programmable inductive elements for superconducting digital and neuromorphic circuits.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates non-volatile spin-valve-controlled resonant frequency shifts in Nb/Co/Nb/Co/Nb/Al split-ring resonators, with a 4 MHz shift at zero field and threefold enhancement via a proximitized Al overlayer, in quantitative agreement with Usadel-equation-based modeling.
AI.motivation: Superconductor-ferromagnet hybrid structures with tunable kinetic inductance are promising for neuromorphic and quantum computing circuits, and the study aims to demonstrate a non-volatile spin-valve effect on resonant properties in such structures.
AI.method: Fabrication and microwave characterization of split-ring resonators based on Nb/Co/Nb/Co/Nb/Al spin-trigger multilayers, with measurement of resonant frequency shifts upon reversing Co layer magnetization orientation.
AI.result: A reproducible zero-field resonant frequency shift of up to 4 MHz was observed, corresponding to a change in kinetic inductance. A proximitized Al overlayer enhanced the inductance contrast between parallel and antiparallel magnetic states by a factor of ~3. Results quantitatively agree with the Usadel-equation-based microscopic model.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic memory of the resonant frequency at zero field establishes spin-trigger multilayers as viable field-programmable inductive elements for superconducting digital and neuromorphic circuits.

title: Puzzling superconductivity in strontium ruthenate: then and now
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, Accepted for publication. Low Temperature Physics (AIP)
summary: Strontium ruthenate is a very interesting low temperature superconductor with relatively simple normal state and very puzzling superconducting state properties. Despite over thirty years of intensive research, even the precise symmetry of the order parameter is not known. In this paper we briefly review some of the key developments, focussing on some of the newer experiments, especially those which challenged the previous understanding that it is a spin triplet odd parity chiral p-wave superconductor. Since Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ now appears most probably a spin singlet superconductor we have calculated the Kerr effect for one candidate $d$-wave pairing state. We find that for the chiral $d$-wave $E_g$ pairing state the calculated Hall conductance is non-zero and qualitatively similar to that found earlier under the assumption of a chiral p-wave $E_u$ order parameter. We characterize the Hall conductance in relation to two sum rules, one related to Berry curvatures in the Bogoliubov quasiparticle states, and the other $f$-sum rule indicating the presence of inter-orbital pairing.

AI.tldr: The paper reviews Sr₂RuO₄, a superconductor under debate, and calculates Kerr effect for a candidate d-wave pairing state, finding non-zero Hall conductance similar to chiral p-wave predictions.
AI.motivation: Despite 30+ years of research, the order parameter symmetry of Sr₂RuO₄ remains unknown. New experiments challenge the previously accepted spin-triplet chiral p-wave picture, motivating investigation of alternative pairing symmetries.
AI.method: The authors calculate the Kerr effect and Hall conductance for a chiral d-wave (E_g) pairing state in Sr₂RuO₄, and characterize the Hall conductance using Berry curvature sum rules (related to Bogoliubov quasiparticles) and the f-sum rule (indicating inter-orbital pairing).
AI.result: For the chiral d-wave E_g pairing state, the calculated Hall conductance is non-zero and qualitatively similar to that previously found for the chiral p-wave E_u order parameter.
AI.conclusion: The chiral d-wave E_g state is a viable candidate for Sr₂RuO₄'s superconducting order parameter, and the Kerr effect alone cannot distinguish between chiral p-wave and chiral d-wave pairing in this system.

title: Driven criticality links universal computation and optimal representations
summary: Near-critical dynamics are often linked to enhanced computation, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. We address this question in reservoir computing, where a fixed recurrent network maps input sequences into high-dimensional states and only a simple readout is trained. We extend fixed-reservoir universality results to discrete-time input-driven reservoirs and connect their key geometric condition, neighborhood separation, to dynamics. To this end, we introduce a finite-resolution neighborhood separability index and an input-conditioned maximal Lyapunov exponent. We find that neighborhood separability, chaotic time-series prediction, and smooth high-dimensional representation geometry are optimized in the same narrow window of marginal driven stability. In this regime, the covariance spectrum approaches the power-law scaling expected for near-optimal smooth representations. Our results link edge-of-instability computation, universality, readout performance, and optimal representation geometry within a common dynamical framework.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates why near-critical (edge-of-instability) dynamics enhance computation in reservoir computing. It extends universality results, introduces a neighborhood separability index and input-conditioned Lyapunov exponent, and shows that optimal performance in chaotic prediction, separability, and representation geometry all emerge in the same narrow window of marginal driven stability, where the covariance spectrum follows power-law scaling.
AI.motivation: Near-critical dynamics are known to enhance computation in recurrent networks, but the underlying mechanism is unclear. The authors aim to explain this phenomenon within reservoir computing by linking dynamical properties to computational performance and representation geometry.
AI.method: The authors extend fixed-reservoir universality results to discrete-time input-driven reservoirs, introduce a finite-resolution neighborhood separability index and an input-conditioned maximal Lyapunov exponent, and analyze the covariance spectrum scaling of reservoir states.
AI.result: Neighborhood separability, chaotic time-series prediction, and smooth high-dimensional representation geometry are all optimized in the same narrow window of marginal driven stability. In this regime, the covariance spectrum exhibits power-law scaling, indicative of near-optimal smooth representations.
AI.conclusion: Edge-of-instability computation, universality, readout performance, and optimal representation geometry are all linked within a common dynamical framework, providing a mechanistic explanation for enhanced computation near criticality.

title: A framework for general discrete probability calculations
summary: Probability follows a simple and concise set of rules. In practice, however, reason- ing about probability may be highly unintuitive and this leads to the possibility of miscalculations even for simple problems. We present an approach to facilitate the correct description of systems governed by discrete probability. The methods described in this paper allow making general statements about the values of prob- ability. This information can next be used to calculate any probability related to the system described by the statements. In case there are too few statements to provide a unique answer, entropy maximization is used to fill in the miss- ing information. The approach has wide potential applications that range from experimental physics to natural language analysis. The theoretical framework described here is also the basis of a software implementation that is designed to be straightforward to extend and requires only popular python libraries, numpy, torch, sympy, and scipy.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a framework using entropy maximization to compute probabilities from partial statements, with applications from physics to NLP, implemented in Python.
AI.motivation: Probability reasoning is often unintuitive and error-prone even for simple problems; a systematic approach is needed to avoid miscalculations.
AI.method: The approach allows making general statements about probability values, then uses entropy maximization to fill missing information when statements are insufficient for a unique answer.
AI.result: The framework enables calculating any probability related to a system described by probabilistic statements, with a Python implementation using numpy, torch, sympy, and scipy.
AI.conclusion: The approach has wide potential across experimental physics and natural language analysis, and the software is designed for easy extensibility.

title: Ideal Bands in Tight-Binding Models
summary: A band is called ideal when its Dirichlet functional saturates the topological lower bound. We study ideal bands in finite-band tight-binding models with conventional two-dimensional lattice translation symmetries, allowing the bands to have non-flat dispersion. We first provide an analytic construction of isolated Chern-ideal bands with Chern number $|\mathrm{Ch}|=1$ in finite-band models with exponentially decaying hopping. This construction applies only when at least two orbitals have different embedded positions (modulo lattice vectors), complementing the previously known construction for $|\mathrm{Ch}|>1$. We then show that isolated Chern-ideal bands with any nonzero Chern number cannot exist in finite-band models with finite-range hopping, regardless of the embedded orbital positions. The conclusion holds even if there are isolated band touching points, as long as the Berry curvature does not diverge anywhere in the Brillouin zone. We finally generalize the conclusions to Wilson-loop-ideal bands with zero total Chern number, such as Kane-Mele $\mathbb{Z}_2$-ideal bands.

AI.tldr: The paper studies ideal bands (where the Dirichlet functional saturates the topological lower bound) in finite-band tight-binding models with 2D lattice translation symmetry. It provides an analytic construction of isolated Chern-ideal bands with |Ch|=1 using exponentially decaying hopping when at least two orbitals have different embedded positions, and proves that such bands cannot exist with finite-range hopping for any nonzero Chern number, extending these results to Wilson-loop-ideal bands like Kane-Mele Z2-ideal bands.
AI.motivation: To understand the constraints on ideal bands in finite-band tight-binding models, specifically whether isolated Chern-ideal bands with |Ch|=1 can exist and under what hopping conditions (exponentially decaying vs. finite-range), and to generalize findings to Wilson-loop-ideal bands.
AI.method: Analytic construction of Chern-ideal bands with |Ch|=1 using exponentially decaying hopping when at least two orbitals have different embedded positions; proof of impossibility for finite-range hopping via analysis of Berry curvature behavior and band structure constraints.
AI.result: (1) An analytic construction of isolated Chern-ideal bands with |Ch|=1 exists for exponentially decaying hopping when at least two orbitals have different embedded positions. (2) Isolated Chern-ideal bands with any nonzero Chern number cannot exist in finite-band models with finite-range hopping, even with isolated band touching points as long as Berry curvature does not diverge. (3) These conclusions generalize to Wilson-loop-ideal bands with zero total Chern number, including Kane-Mele Z2-ideal bands.
AI.conclusion: The existence of Chern-ideal bands with |Ch|=1 requires exponentially decaying hopping and multiple orbitals with different embedded positions, while finite-range hopping precludes any isolated Chern-ideal bands with nonzero Chern number. The results extend to Wilson-loop-ideal bands, providing fundamental constraints on the realizability of ideal bands in lattice models.

title: Monte Carlo Studies of Twisted Bilayer Graphene: Strain and Thermal Fluctuations
summary: We study the phase diagram of twisted bilayer graphene at charge neutrality as a function of twist angle $θ$, uniaxial heterostrain $\varepsilon$, and temperature $T$ using sign-problem-free quantum Monte Carlo simulations. At $T=0$ and zero strain, we find a continuous transition from a Dirac semimetal to a gapped Kramers inter-valley coherent (KIVC) phase as $θ$ decreases toward the magic angle. With finite strain, the KIVC phase undergoes a further continuous transition at smaller $θ$ into an anisotropic semimetal with gapless excitations near the center of the moiré Brillouin zone. In the KIVC regime, the entropy rises sharply with temperature and plateaus at $15\,\text{K} \lesssim T \lesssim 40\,\text{K}$ near the value expected from a Mott-like regime of localized electrons with nearly uncorrelated spin, valley, and orbital degrees of freedom, despite the topological obstruction preventing a localized tight-binding description of the active bands. The spectral function evolves continuously with $θ$: at low $T$, a gap opens at the $K$ points and the minimal gap shifts to $Γ$ as $θ$ decreases; at intermediate $T$, the spectral function smoothly interpolates between a Dirac semimetal spectrum with coherent $K$-point quasiparticles and a spectrum with gapless $Γ$-centered quasiparticles near the magic angle. The later can be a anisotropic or a Mott semimetal and we discuss how to distiguish them in experiment.

AI.tldr: Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations, the paper maps the phase diagram of charge-neutral twisted bilayer graphene as functions of twist angle, strain, and temperature, revealing a continuous transition from Dirac semimetal to KIVC insulator at zero strain, a further transition to an anisotropic semimetal under strain, and a high-temperature entropy plateau indicative of a Mott-like regime with localized electrons.
AI.motivation: To understand the interplay of correlation, topology, and disorder (strain) in the phase diagram of twisted bilayer graphene at charge neutrality, particularly the nature of transitions between semimetal and insulating phases and the role of entropy at finite temperature.
AI.method: Sign-problem-free quantum Monte Carlo simulations of twisted bilayer graphene at charge neutrality, systematic scanning of twist angle θ, uniaxial heterostrain ε, and temperature T.
AI.result: (1) At T=0 and zero strain: continuous Dirac semimetal to KIVC transition as θ decreases. (2) Under finite strain: further continuous transition at smaller θ to an anisotropic semimetal with gapless excitations at moiré Γ. (3) Entropy plateau at 15-40 K in the KIVC regime near the value expected from a Mott-like state with uncorrelated spin/valley/orbital degrees of freedom. (4) Spectral function evolution: gap opens at K then shifts to Γ as θ decreases; gapless Γ-centered quasiparticles near magic angle (anisotropic or Mott semimetal).
AI.conclusion: The phase diagram of neutral TBG is richer than previously appreciated, with strain driving a distinct anisotropic semimetal phase; the high-temperature entropy plateau reveals a Mott-like regime despite topological obstruction to a localized tight-binding description; two types of gapless Γ-centered semimetals exist near the magic angle with experimentally distinguishable signatures.

title: Importance-Sampling Estimation of Gaussian Molecular Shape Overlap: Exact Union Volumes and Confidence-Bounded Virtual Screening
summary: Gaussian descriptions of molecular shape underpin 3D shape-based virtual screening, but existing methods evaluate Gaussian overlap analytically. The widely used first-order approximation is fast but systematically overestimates overlap, whereas the exact molecular volume requires a combinatorial inclusion-exclusion expansion. We introduce the first stochastic estimator of Gaussian shape overlap: an unbiased Monte Carlo method that importance-samples directly from a molecule's Gaussian mixture. The estimator reproduces analytic overlap without bias and extends to the exact union volume of all inclusion-exclusion orders with O(N) cost per sample. On drug-like molecules, the union estimator matches high-resolution grid quadrature with a mean relative error of 0.07 percent, while the first-order approximation overestimates the true union volume by 3.4x on average. The estimator provides analytic standard errors, enabling confidence-bounded screening that reduces sampling by 94 percent while preserving ranking. Implemented in JAX, it is fully differentiable and supports gradient-based rigid alignment on CPU, GPU, and TPU. On the DUD-E and LIT-PCBA benchmarks, the method achieves shape-only enrichment comparable to existing single-conformer approaches while additionally providing unbiased absolute volumes and uncertainty estimates.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a stochastic Monte Carlo estimator for Gaussian shape overlap in 3D molecular shape-based virtual screening. The method is unbiased, handles exact union volume efficiently (O(N) per sample), is fully differentiable (JAX implementation), and provides analytic standard errors enabling confidence-bounded screening with up to 94% sampling reduction while maintaining ranking performance.
AI.motivation: Existing Gaussian shape overlap methods either use a fast but systematically overestimating first-order approximation or require a computationally expensive inclusion-exclusion expansion for exact molecular volume. The authors sought an unbiased, efficient, and scalable estimator that can handle both pairwise overlap and exact union volume while providing uncertainty quantification.
AI.method: An unbiased Monte Carlo method that importance-samples directly from a molecule's Gaussian mixture density. It computes pairwise overlap by sampling from one molecule's density and evaluating the ratio of the other's density. For union volume, it extends the estimator to all inclusion-exclusion orders with O(N) cost per sample. Implemented in JAX for differentiability and hardware portability (CPU/GPU/TPU).
AI.result: The union estimator matches high-resolution grid quadrature with 0.07% mean relative error on drug-like molecules, while the first-order approximation overestimates true union volume by 3.4x on average. Confidence-bounded screening reduces sampling by 94% while preserving ranking. Shape-only enrichment on DUD-E and LIT-PCBA benchmarks is comparable to existing single-conformer approaches.
AI.conclusion: The proposed stochastic estimator provides unbiased, efficient, and differentiable Gaussian shape overlap computations with built-in uncertainty quantification, offering a principled alternative to biased first-order approximations for 3D shape-based virtual screening.

title: A Single-Trace Surface Integral Equation Solver for Simulation of Open Bianisotropic Metasurfaces Described by Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions
summary: A single-trace surface integral equation (SIE) solver incorporating generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) is presented for the simulation of three-dimensional (3D) open bianisotropic metasurfaces. The metasurface is modeled as an infinitesimally thin, non-enclosing sheet across which the GSTCs enforce the electromagnetic field discontinuities through four surface susceptibility tensors. The proposed solver uses a single set of equivalent surface currents on the sheet, in place of the two sets used by prior multi-trace formulations. The scattered fields on both faces of the sheet, expressed through SIE operators acting on these currents, are substituted into the GSTCs. The resulting system of equations is then discretized using Rao--Wilton--Glisson basis functions. This solver models an open metasurface directly, without an artificial closure, and applies to both planar and curved geometries. It is validated against analytical solutions for polarization rotation and perfect reflection, and is used to model a realistic broadband absorber whose susceptibility tensors are retrieved from full-wave simulation data. A direct comparison shows that the single-trace formulation attains lower error than a multi-trace formulation while using significantly fewer unknowns.

AI.tldr: A single-trace surface integral equation solver using generalized sheet transition conditions is presented for simulating 3D open bianisotropic metasurfaces. It uses one set of equivalent surface currents instead of two, models open surfaces without artificial closure, works for planar and curved geometries, and achieves lower error with fewer unknowns than multi-trace formulations.
AI.motivation: To develop a more efficient and accurate computational method for simulating open bianisotropic metasurfaces by eliminating the need for artificial closures and reducing the number of unknown current sets compared to existing multi-trace formulations.
AI.method: A single-trace SIE solver incorporating GSTCs, using a single set of equivalent surface currents on an infinitesimally thin sheet. Scattered fields on both faces are expressed via SIE operators on these currents and substituted into GSTCs. The system is discretized using Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions.
AI.result: Validated against analytical solutions for polarization rotation and perfect reflection. Applied to model a broadband absorber with susceptibility tensors from full-wave data. The single-trace formulation attains lower error than a multi-trace formulation while using significantly fewer unknowns.
AI.conclusion: The proposed single-trace GSTC-SIE solver provides a more efficient and accurate approach for simulating open bianisotropic metasurfaces, applicable to both planar and curved geometries without requiring artificial closure.

title: Entanglement asymmetry and quantum Mpemba effect for Kramers-Wannier duality
summary: The Kramers-Wannier duality is the prototypical example of a non-invertible symmetry, yet little is known about its fate away from criticality and out of equilibrium. We introduce the Kramers-Wannier entanglement asymmetry, a quantum-information measure that quantifies the breaking of this non-invertible symmetry in the transverse-field Ising chain. We first investigate its equilibrium properties, showing that it exhibits a striking crossover between the ordered and disordered phases together with a pronounced dip at the critical point that becomes increasingly sharp with subsystem size. We then study quantum quenches from both gapped phases to criticality and show that the Kramers-Wannier entanglement asymmetry decays to zero, signaling the dynamical restoration of the non-invertible symmetry. Remarkably, we uncover the emergence of a quantum Mpemba effect: under suitable conditions, states initially farther from equilibrium restore the Kramers-Wannier symmetry faster than states prepared closer to it. We provide both analytical and numerical evidence for this phenomenon and identify the mechanism responsible for its occurrence. Our work establishes entanglement asymmetry as a powerful probe of non-invertible symmetries beyond equilibrium and opens new perspectives on the dynamics of dualities in quantum many-body systems.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Kramers-Wannier entanglement asymmetry to probe non-invertible symmetry breaking in the transverse-field Ising chain, revealing a crossover between phases, a sharp dip at criticality, dynamical symmetry restoration after quenches, and a quantum Mpemba effect where states farther from equilibrium restore symmetry faster.
AI.motivation: Little is known about the fate of non-invertible symmetries (like Kramers-Wannier duality) away from criticality and out of equilibrium; the authors aim to develop a quantum-information probe to fill this gap.
AI.method: The authors define the Kramers-Wannier entanglement asymmetry, a quantum-information measure quantifying the breaking of the non-invertible symmetry. They analyze it analytically and numerically in equilibrium (ordered/disordered phases, critical point) and after quantum quenches from gapped phases to criticality.
AI.result: The asymmetry shows a crossover between ordered and disordered phases, a sharp dip at criticality that grows with subsystem size, and decays to zero after quenches signaling dynamical symmetry restoration. A quantum Mpemba effect is discovered: certain initial states farther from equilibrium restore the symmetry faster.
AI.conclusion: Entanglement asymmetry is a powerful probe of non-invertible symmetries beyond equilibrium, offering new insights into the dynamics of dualities in quantum many-body systems.

title: Lithium-Projected Phonon Spectral Distributions as Robust Descriptors of Ionic Conductivity in Solid Electrolytes
summary: Lattice dynamics are widely invoked in the design of solid electrolytes, yet phonon information is commonly compressed into a band center or another scalar softness measure. Here we test whether the complete lithium-projected phonon density of states (Li-PDOS) provides a reproducible descriptor of experimental room-temperature ionic conductivity. MatterSim forces and Phonopy were used to generate harmonic total and Li-projected spectra for crystallographically resolved entries in the OBELiX dataset. A composition and structure audit defined a primary cohort of 260 materials (212 train and 48 test), a strict cohort of 241, and an exact-composition cohort of 168. Across 20 independently generated phonon-calculation database comparisons, the mean Wasserstein-1 distance was 0.542 THz for total DOS and 0.731 THz for Li-PDOS, revealing broad agreement but systematic, projection-dependent softening. Higher conductivity was associated with redistribution of normalized Li spectral weight toward low frequencies: in the untouched test set, the Li fractions below 2 and 5 THz had Spearman coefficients of 0.333 and 0.374, while the 5$\%$ cumulative-frequency quantile had a coefficient of $-0.393$. A Wasserstein kernel on the full Li-PDOS achieved held-out $R^2=0.444$, compared with 0.012 for total DOS and 0.181 for a static composition--structure kernel. The Li model remained stable in the strict ($R^2=0.462$) and exact ($R^2=0.451$) cohorts. Family adjustment attenuated scalar associations, and Li-versus-total whole-spectrum dependence was cohort sensitive. The results therefore support mobile-ion-resolved spectral distributions as useful comparative screening descriptors, not as a universal causal softness law.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether lithium-projected phonon density of states (Li-PDOS) serves as a reproducible descriptor of room-temperature ionic conductivity in solid electrolytes. Using MatterSim forces and Phonopy on the OBELiX dataset, the authors find that Li-PDOS features (especially low-frequency weight) correlate with conductivity (R²=0.444 with Wasserstein kernel) and outperform total DOS or static descriptors. However, results are cohort-sensitive and family-attenuated, supporting Li-PDOS as a comparative screening descriptor rather than a universal causal law.
AI.motivation: Lattice dynamics are commonly used in solid electrolyte design, but phonon information is typically compressed into scalar softness measures (e.g., band center). The authors aim to test whether the full lithium-projected phonon density of states provides a more informative and reproducible descriptor of experimental ionic conductivity.
AI.method: The authors used MatterSim forces and Phonopy to compute harmonic total and Li-projected phonon DOS for crystallographically resolved entries in the OBELiX dataset. Three cohorts were defined: primary (260 materials), strict (241), and exact-composition (168). Wasserstein-1 distance assessed inter-database reproducibility. Spearman correlations and Wasserstein kernel regression (with held-out R²) were used to relate Li-PDOS features to experimental conductivity.
AI.result: Mean Wasserstein-1 distances were 0.542 THz (total DOS) and 0.731 THz (Li-PDOS), showing broad agreement with systematic projection-dependent softening. Higher conductivity correlated with Li spectral weight redistribution toward low frequencies: Spearman coefficients of 0.333 (below 2 THz) and 0.374 (below 5 THz). A Wasserstein kernel on Li-PDOS achieved held-out R²=0.444, outperforming total DOS (R²=0.012) and static composition–structure kernels (R²=0.181). Results remained stable in strict (R²=0.462) and exact (R²=0.451) cohorts.
AI.conclusion: The Li-PDOS is a useful comparative screening descriptor for ionic conductivity, but it is not a universal causal softness law. The approach is cohort-sensitive and family-attenuated, meaning results depend on the dataset composition and must be interpreted with care.

title: Measurement of the reduced dipole matrix element in Ba$^+$
summary: We present a high-precision measurement of the reduced electric-dipole matrix element $\langle P_{1/2}\|r\|S_{1/2}\rangle$ in $^{138}\mathrm{Ba}^+$. By comparing off-resonant scattering rates with dispersive Stark-shift measurements, we determine the matrix element to be $3.322\,7(12)$, corresponding to a $P_{1/2}$ excited-state radiative lifetime of $7.866\,3(56)$~ns. Combining our experimental results with a prior model for the differential scalar polarizability $Δα_0(ω)$, we extract the static value $Δα_0(0) = -73.09(12)$a.u. This determination directly improves the evaluation of the blackbody radiation (BBR) shift, minimizing a prominent systematic limitation in room-temperature $\mathrm{Ba}^+$ optical clock error budgets. These results provide a stringent benchmark for atomic-structure calculations and advance high-precision applications in quantum metrology and tests of fundamental physics.

AI.tldr: High-precision measurement of the Ba⁺ electric-dipole matrix element ⟨P₁/₂∥r∥S₁/₂⟩ = 3.3227(12), yielding P₁/₂ radiative lifetime = 7.8663(56) ns and static differential polarizability Δα₀(0) = -73.09(12) a.u., reducing BBR shift uncertainty for Ba⁺ optical clocks.
AI.motivation: To improve Ba⁺ optical clock accuracy by precisely determining the BBR shift, a key systematic limitation in room-temperature operation, and to provide a benchmark for atomic-structure calculations.
AI.method: Comparison of off-resonant scattering rates with dispersive Stark-shift measurements to extract the reduced dipole matrix element, combined with a prior model for Δα₀(ω) to obtain the static polarizability.
AI.result: Matrix element = 3.3227(12), P₁/₂ lifetime = 7.8663(56) ns, static Δα₀(0) = -73.09(12) a.u.
AI.conclusion: The measurement reduces BBR shift uncertainty in Ba⁺ optical clocks, provides a stringent benchmark for atomic theory, and advances applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics tests.

title: Supercurrent effect in a charge density wave intertwined superconductor
comment: Main text: 20 pages, 4 figures; Supplementary Information: 27 pages, 17 figures
summary: The energy-momentum (E-k) dispersion of quasiparticles constitutes a fundamental concept in condensed matter systems. The ability to modify the E-k dispersion, exemplified by supercurrent-induced Doppler shifts of Bogoliubov quasiparticle spectra in superconductors, enables manipulation of various emergent quantum properties. However, investigations into the supercurrent effect on superconductors intertwined with charge orders remain scarce. Here, we report that the Meissner current, generated by the diamagnetic response to an applied in-plane magnetic field, can tailor Bogoliubov quasiparticle excitations at the precursor charge density wave (CDW) vectors. Our scanning tunneling spectroscopic imaging reveals a field-driven symmetry breaking of CDW modulations, specifically a C3v-to-Cs transition, in superconducting NbSe2. Model calculations suggest that the observed anisotropy originates from a selective Doppler-shift-induced E-k dispersion reconstruction. Furthermore, altering the field direction enables on-demand tuning of anisotropic CDW modulations and visualization of their momentum-space distribution. These results highlight a novel mechanism for controlling emergent electronic phases through momentum-space engineering.

AI.tldr: Meissner current from an in-plane magnetic field induces a C3v-to-Cs symmetry breaking of charge density wave modulations in superconducting NbSe2 via selective Doppler-shift-induced reconstruction of quasiparticle energy-momentum dispersion, enabling on-demand control of anisotropic CDW order.
AI.motivation: Despite known supercurrent-induced Doppler shifts of Bogoliubov quasiparticles in superconductors, the effect of supercurrent on superconductors coexisting with charge order (like CDW) remains poorly understood, motivating the study of how Meissner current tailors quasiparticle excitations at CDW vectors.
AI.method: Scanning tunneling spectroscopic imaging was used to observe field-driven symmetry breaking of CDW modulations in superconducting NbSe2 under an in-plane magnetic field; model calculations were performed to attribute the anisotropy to Doppler-shift-induced E-k dispersion reconstruction.
AI.result: A C3v-to-Cs symmetry transition of CDW modulations was observed in NbSe2 driven by the Meissner current orientation; anisotropic CDW modulations could be tuned on demand by altering the field direction, enabling visualization of momentum-space distribution.
AI.conclusion: These results demonstrate a novel mechanism for controlling emergent electronic phases via momentum-space engineering, specifically through Doppler-shift-induced dispersion reconstruction by supercurrents.

title: Uni-XAS: Alignment-Driven Bidirectional Multimodal Learning for X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
comment: 48 pages, 7 figures, 11 tables. Accepted by ACMMM 2026
summary: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is a key technique for probing local atomic environments, yet learning based modeling must bridge two heterogeneous modalities: 1D continuous spectra and 3D atomic structures. Existing approaches typically decouple forward spectrum prediction and inverse structure inference into separate regression tasks, hindering shared representation learning. Moreover, severe permutation ambiguity among identical atoms often limits inverse modeling to coarse structure descriptors rather than explicit 3D structure generation. In this work, we present Uni-XAS, a unified benchmark and learning framework that reframes bidirectional XAS modeling as a cross-modal alignment and conditional generation problem. We first propose XASLip, an alignment recipe coupling a physics-aware spectral encoder with an absorberaware manifold optimization strategy to resolve fine-grained intra-element coordination variations. Building upon this shared latent space, we formulate forward prediction as anchored absolute-spectrum generation via retrieval-augmented decoding, effectively preventing physical scale collapse and energy drift. For the inherently ill-posed inverse problem, we introduce Permutation-Rectified Flow Matching, which integrates type-wise optimal transport into a continuous generative flow to provide a principled solution to ligand permutation ambiguity without relying on heavy high-order equivariant architectures. Evaluated on a largescale standardized benchmark of 328,839 structure-spectrum pairs, Uni-XAS demonstrates strong performance in cross-modal retrieval, accurate absolute-spectrum prediction, and composition-conditional 3D structure generation, establishing a scalable, reproducible, and protocol-consistent foundation for multimodal learning and standardized evaluation in scientific spectroscopy.

AI.tldr: Uni-XAS is a unified benchmark and learning framework for bidirectional X-ray absorption spectroscopy modeling that uses cross-modal alignment (XASLip) and conditional generation (Permutation-Rectified Flow Matching) to bridge 1D spectra and 3D atomic structures, demonstrating strong performance on a large-scale benchmark of 328,839 structure-spectrum pairs.
AI.motivation: Existing XAS modeling approaches treat forward spectrum prediction and inverse structure inference as separate regression tasks, failing to leverage shared representations. Additionally, inverse modeling is hindered by permutation ambiguity among identical atoms, limiting it to coarse structure descriptors rather than explicit 3D structure generation.
AI.method: Uni-XAS proposes (1) XASLip: a cross-modal alignment recipe coupling a physics-aware spectral encoder with absorber-aware manifold optimization; (2) retrieval-augmented decoding for anchored absolute-spectrum generation in forward prediction; (3) Permutation-Rectified Flow Matching using type-wise optimal transport within a continuous generative flow for inverse structure generation, avoiding heavy equivariant architectures.
AI.result: Evaluated on 328,839 structure-spectrum pairs, Uni-XAS achieves strong performance in cross-modal retrieval, accurate absolute-spectrum prediction, and composition-conditional 3D structure generation.
AI.conclusion: Uni-XAS establishes a scalable, reproducible, and protocol-consistent foundation for multimodal learning and standardized evaluation in scientific spectroscopy.

title: High Order Geometric Channels for Nonlinear Transport in Bloch Bands
summary: We develop a geometric perturbation theory of Bloch states for perturbations coupling via the interband Berry connection. The gauge-invariant Bargmann trace builds the dressed dispersion and connection order by order as a hierarchy \(Q^{(N)}\), starting with the quantum geometric tensor. Higher members encode multiband geometry beyond the quantum metric and Berry curvature. Connected amplitudes control vertex-order corrections, while strict-order corrections reduce to disconnected products. For a uniform electric field we find the fully coherent, purely geometric sector of the third-order response.

AI.tldr: A geometric perturbation theory for Bloch states is developed using the interband Berry connection, leading to a hierarchy \(Q^{(N)}\) that generalizes the quantum geometric tensor. Higher-order terms capture multiband geometry beyond quantum metric and Berry curvature, with connected amplitudes governing vertex corrections and disconnected products giving strict-order corrections. For a uniform electric field, the purely geometric sector of third-order response is identified.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic perturbation theory for Bloch states under perturbations that couple through the interband Berry connection, extending beyond the quantum geometric tensor to capture higher-order multiband geometric effects.
AI.method: A gauge-invariant Bargmann trace is used to construct the dressed dispersion and connection order by order as a hierarchy \(Q^{(N)}\). Connected amplitudes control vertex-order corrections while strict-order corrections reduce to disconnected products.
AI.result: The fully coherent, purely geometric sector of the third-order response is found for a uniform electric field.
AI.conclusion: The hierarchy \(Q^{(N)}\) systematically captures multiband geometry beyond the quantum metric and Berry curvature, with clear separation of connected and disconnected contributions, and yields a purely geometric third-order response under a uniform electric field.

title: Colloquium: Semi-Dirac Fermions in Quantum Matter
comment: Submitted to Reviews of Modern Physics
summary: This article reviews the recent progress on the subject of semi-Dirac fermions, two dimensional quasiparticles that disperse quadratically, as Galilean invariant particles, or linearly, as massless relativistic particles, depending on their direction of motion. These particles exist at a phase boundary set by the continuous change in the connectivity of Fermi surfaces, known as topological Lifshitz transitions. The basic properties and the current experimental evidence of the existence of these particles in both synthetic lattices and quantum materials are presented. The many-body problem of semi-Dirac fermions is discussed from a theoretical perspective with an eye to physical observables of relevance to experiments.

AI.tldr: This review covers semi-Dirac fermions—2D quasiparticles with direction-dependent quadratic (Galilean) or linear (relativistic) dispersion—that emerge at topological Lifshitz transitions. It summarizes their properties, experimental evidence in synthetic lattices and quantum materials, and theoretical many-body effects relevant to experiments.
AI.motivation: To provide a consolidated review of semi-Dirac fermions, a class of quasiparticles with unique anisotropic dispersion that bridges Galilean and relativistic regimes, which emerge at topological Lifshitz transitions. The goal is to present current experimental evidence and theoretical many-body perspectives to guide future research.
AI.method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental findings in synthetic lattices (e.g., photonic, cold-atom systems) and quantum materials, alongside theoretical analysis of many-body interactions, emphasizing physical observables.
AI.result: Semi-Dirac fermions exhibit a Lifshitz transition where the Fermi surface topology changes continuously, leading to anisotropic quasiparticle behavior (quadratic in one direction, linear in the orthogonal direction). Experimental evidence has been reported in both engineered synthetic lattices and natural quantum materials.
AI.conclusion: Semi-Dirac fermions represent a distinct phase boundary state in 2D systems, with unique anisotropic transport and many-body properties that are accessible to experiment, motivating further exploration in both artificial and real materials.

title: Determination of fundamental properties of nitrogen from first principles. I. Atomic polarizabilities and long-range dispersion coefficients
summary: This work is the first in a series of papers in which we perform theoretical calculations of various fundamental properties of nitrogen relevant for gas thermometry experiments. In this part we focus on the properties of nitrogen atom, namely dynamic polarizabilities and dispersion coefficients that describe interaction between two nitrogen atoms at large internuclear separations. These quantities are calculated using a composite scheme based on coupled cluster and full configuration interaction methods and large Gaussian basis sets optimized specifically for the purposes of this work. The dispersion coefficients, $C_n$ with $n=6,8,10$, are obtained using Casimir--Polder formulas by numerical integration over dipole, quadrupole, and octuple polarizabilities for imaginary frequencies represented analytically by Padé approximants. Special attention is paid to careful error control and uncertainty estimation of the calculated quantities.

AI.tldr: This paper presents theoretical calculations of dynamic polarizabilities and dispersion coefficients (C6, C8, C10) for nitrogen atoms using coupled cluster and full configuration interaction methods with optimized Gaussian basis sets, focusing on error control and uncertainty estimation for gas thermometry applications.
AI.motivation: To provide accurate theoretical data on nitrogen atom properties (polarizabilities and dispersion coefficients) needed for gas thermometry experiments, as part of a series on fundamental nitrogen properties.
AI.method: A composite scheme employing coupled cluster and full configuration interaction methods with large, specially optimized Gaussian basis sets; dispersion coefficients are computed via Casimir-Polder formulas through numerical integration of dipole, quadrupole, and octuple polarizabilities at imaginary frequencies, analytically represented by Padé approximants.
AI.result: Dynamic polarizabilities and dispersion coefficients C6, C8, C10 for nitrogen atoms at large internuclear separations, with careful uncertainty estimation.
AI.conclusion: The computed quantities provide reliable reference data for gas thermometry, with rigorous error control and uncertainty quantification ensuring their usefulness for experimental applications.

title: Matrix-free phase-field modeling of fracture in micromechanical testing simulations of inelastic materials
summary: Resolving steep damage gradients across diffuse cracks in the phase-field modeling of fracture favors the use of high-order finite elements, for which matrix-free methods can provide superior performance and scalability. Here, we implement the Peric & Dettmer constitutive framework for visco-elastoplastic materials in an open source solid mechanics library supporting matrix-free operators for high-order finite elements with p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs. We introduce a rheological fracture element assembled in series so that inelastic and fracture properties can appear to affect each other only at homogenization length scales. Numerical simulations of tensile and compressive tests are conducted for synthetic particle-matrix microstructures on an El Capitan high performance computing prototype. Results are shown to reproduce characteristic inelastic responses and crack propagation patterns.

AI.tldr: The paper implements a visco-elastoplastic constitutive framework with phase-field fracture modeling using high-order finite elements with matrix-free methods and p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs, demonstrating effective simulation of inelastic responses and crack propagation in particle-matrix microstructures on an El Capitan HPC prototype.
AI.motivation: To address steep damage gradients across diffuse cracks in phase-field fracture modeling, high-order finite elements are preferred, and matrix-free methods can offer superior performance and scalability for such computations.
AI.method: The Peric & Dettmer visco-elastoplastic constitutive framework is implemented in an open-source solid mechanics library supporting matrix-free operators for high-order finite elements with p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs. A rheological fracture element assembled in series is introduced so that inelastic and fracture properties interact only at homogenization length scales.
AI.result: Numerical simulations of tensile and compressive tests on synthetic particle-matrix microstructures on an El Capitan HPC prototype successfully reproduce characteristic inelastic responses and crack propagation patterns.
AI.conclusion: The proposed GPU-accelerated, high-order finite element approach with matrix-free operators and p-multigrid preconditioning is effective for phase-field modeling of fracture in visco-elastoplastic materials.

title: Thermal pseudo-transitions in a frustrated spin-pseudospin sawtooth chain
summary: We present an exact analysis of a spin--pseudospin X sawtooth chain that incorporates three distinct valence states of copper ions and serves as a minimal model for one-dimensional cuprates composed of corner-sharing copper triangles. The model includes magnetic exchange and electrostatic coupling constants both along the base sites and between base and apex sites capturing the competition between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Using the transfer-matrix method, we derive exact expressions for the free energy and obtain an analytical condition defining the pseudo-critical line associated with pronounced thermodynamic anomalies. The ground-state analysis reveals, besides an antiferromagnetic phase, three frustrated phases characterized by distinct residual entropies. At finite temperatures, these zero-temperature phase boundaries evolve into narrow entropy ridges signaling pseudo-transitions between the corresponding quasi-phases. The specific heat and the avoided-crossing scale exhibit sharp but continuous peaks at the pseudo-critical temperature, whereas the physical correlation length may be controlled by a different subleading eigenvalue. Local correlation functions uncover a cooperative rearrangement from charge-dominated to magnetically correlated regimes. Our results demonstrate that the sawtooth geometry promotes frustration and short-range coherence leading to pronounced pseudo-transition behavior.

AI.tldr: Exact analysis of a spin-pseudospin X sawtooth chain model for 1D cuprates, using transfer-matrix method to derive free energy, pseudo-critical lines, and reveal three frustrated phases with residual entropies, pseudo-transitions, and charge-to-magnetic regime crossover.
AI.motivation: To provide a minimal exactly solvable model for one-dimensional cuprates composed of corner-sharing copper triangles, capturing the competition between spin and charge degrees of freedom and the role of sawtooth geometry in promoting frustration.
AI.method: Transfer-matrix method for exact derivation of free energy and analytical pseudo-critical conditions; ground-state and finite-temperature analysis of phase boundaries, entropy ridges, specific heat, avoided-crossing scale, and local correlation functions.
AI.result: Identified one antiferromagnetic and three frustrated phases with distinct residual entropies at zero temperature; finite-temperature pseudo-transitions with sharp but continuous specific heat peaks; physical correlation length governed by a subleading eigenvalue; charge-to-magnetic cooperative rearrangement observed.
AI.conclusion: The sawtooth geometry inherently promotes frustration and short-range coherence, leading to pronounced pseudo-transition behavior, demonstrating the rich physics accessible in this exactly solvable minimal model.

authors: Herr S. J. van der Zant
title: Magnetic ground states of CrPS$_4$ and NiPS$_3$ monolayers from long-range exchange interactions
summary: We investigate the magnetic properties of monolayer CrPS$_4$ and NiPS$_3$ by combining first-principles calculations, second-principles spin models, and Monte Carlo simulations. Unlike conventional approaches that truncate exchange interactions after only a few shells and determine them by fitting total energies, we extract the magnetic exchange tensors directly from density functional theory using the LKAG formalism and include interactions until numerical convergence is achieved. We show that long-range exchange interactions qualitatively modify the magnetic behavior of both materials. In CrPS$_4$, they destabilize the previously predicted ferromagnetic ground state and stabilize a spin-spiral phase, reducing the critical temperature to about 21\,K, in agreement with available experiments. The resulting magnetic phase diagram contains multiple collinear and non-collinear phases that can be tuned by temperature and external magnetic fields. In NiPS$_3$, the experimentally observed zigzag antiferromagnetic order only emerges when exchange interactions up to the fifth shell are included. These results demonstrate that quantitatively predictive spin models for thiophosphate monolayers require long-range exchange interactions and provide a predictive framework for accurately describing two-dimensional van der Waals magnets.

AI.tldr: Using first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations with long-range exchange interactions (via LKAG formalism), the authors show that CrPS₄ favors a spin-spiral phase over ferromagnetism (Tc ≈ 21 K) and that NiPS₃'s zigzag antiferromagnetic order requires up to fifth-shell interactions, demonstrating that long-range exchange is essential for predictive models of 2D thiophosphate magnets.
AI.motivation: Conventional approaches truncate exchange interactions to a few shells and fit them to total energies, which may miss physics critical for correctly describing 2D van der Waals magnets. The authors aim to show that long-range exchange interactions are essential for quantitatively predictive magnetic models of monolayer thiophosphates.
AI.method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) combined with the LKAG formalism to extract magnetic exchange tensors directly, without truncation to few shells. Second-principles spin models and Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute finite-temperature magnetic properties.
AI.result: In CrPS₄, long-range interactions destabilize the previously predicted ferromagnetic ground state, stabilizing a spin-spiral phase with Tc ≈ 21 K, consistent with experiments. In NiPS₃, zigzag antiferromagnetic order only emerges when exchange up to the fifth shell is included.
AI.conclusion: Quantitatively predictive spin models for thiophosphate monolayers must include long-range exchange interactions. The work provides a predictive framework for accurately describing two-dimensional van der Waals magnets.

title: Reassessment of line profile asymmetry in measurements of the 1s-2s energy interval in hydrogen
summary: Experiments to determine transition frequencies in the hydrogen atom represent some of the most precise spectroscopic measurements and are at a higher level among simple atomic systems. The most persistent measured value in hydrogen is the energy interval corresponding to the $1s-2s$ two-photon transition. The achieved experimental precision is several parts of $10^{-15}$ and has not changed over the last two decades. Although repeated experiments in 2011 and 2013 have improved the accuracy by several times, the frequency value has not changed significantly. On this basis, the frequency of the $1s-2s$ transition holds pivotal for determining physical quantities such as the Rydberg constant and the proton charge radius. Theoretical efforts to study in detail the effects that might influence such precise measurements have not revealed significant contributions. The present work revises the theoretical analysis of the line contour asymmetry and its influence on the determination of the two-photon absorption transition frequency, taking into account the theoretical achievements of recent years in this direction. It is shown that the asymmetry of the observed profile can lead to a $1s-2s$ transition frequency shift at the level of modern experimental accuracy. The found frequency shift is consistent with the line shape model contribution that forms the error budget of the experimental measurements. Adjustment can be carried out on the basis of the asymmetric profile that has become standard in recent years.

AI.tldr: This paper revises the theoretical analysis of line contour asymmetry in hydrogen $1s-2s$ two-photon transition, showing that profile asymmetry can cause a frequency shift at the level of modern experimental precision (~$10^{-15}$), consistent with the error budget of current measurements and potentially impacting determinations of the Rydberg constant and proton charge radius.
AI.motivation: The $1s-2s$ transition frequency in hydrogen is among the most precise spectroscopic measurements (parts in $10^{-15}$) and is crucial for determining fundamental constants like the Rydberg constant and proton charge radius. Despite repeated experiments (2011, 2013) improving accuracy, the frequency value has remained stable, and no significant theoretical contributions explaining possible shifts have been identified — motivating a refined theoretical analysis of line shape asymmetry.
AI.method: The authors perform a theoretical revision of the line contour asymmetry analysis for the $1s-2s$ two-photon absorption transition, incorporating recent theoretical achievements in line shape modeling. They quantify how profile asymmetry shifts the determined transition frequency relative to a symmetric model.
AI.result: The asymmetry of the observed profile can lead to a $1s-2s$ transition frequency shift at the level of modern experimental accuracy (~$10^{-15}$). The found shift is consistent with the line shape model contribution already included in the error budget of experimental measurements.
AI.conclusion: The frequency shift from line contour asymmetry is significant at current experimental precision. Adjustment of the $1s-2s$ transition frequency can be carried out using the asymmetric profile model, which has become standard in recent years.

title: Sequential Topological Superconductivity in a Square Lattice with Chiral Charge Density Waves
summary: The interplay between charge order and superconductivity offers a fertile ground for emergent quantum phases. Here we theoretically investigate a square-lattice superconductor coexisting with a composite charge density wave (CDW) consisting of a real bond modulation (charge bond order, CBO) and an imaginary hopping modulation (chiral flux phase, CFP) that breaks time-reversal symmetry. We uncover that, while CFP alone does not induce topology in square lattices, its coexistence with CBO drives the system into two topologically nontrivial superconducting phases with Chern numbers $C=+2$ and $C=-2$. The low-temperature thermal Hall conductivity $κ_{xy}$ exhibits quantized plateaus proportional to the Chern number, providing a clear experimental fingerprint. Our results establish the square lattice as a pristine platform for engineering topological superconductivity through the synergy of real and imaginary bond modulations.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that coexistence of real (CBO) and imaginary (CFP) bond modulations in a square-lattice superconductor induces topological superconducting phases with Chern numbers C=±2, detectable via quantized thermal Hall conductivity plateaus.
AI.motivation: To explore how the interplay between charge order (specifically composite CDW with real and imaginary components) and superconductivity can generate topological quantum phases in a square lattice system.
AI.method: Theoretical investigation of a square-lattice superconductor coexisting with a composite charge density wave featuring real bond modulation (CBO) and imaginary hopping modulation (CFP) that breaks time-reversal symmetry.
AI.result: CFP alone does not induce topology, but its coexistence with CBO drives two topologically nontrivial superconducting phases with Chern numbers C=+2 and C=-2, with quantized thermal Hall conductivity κ_xy plateaus proportional to the Chern number.
AI.conclusion: The square lattice serves as a pristine platform for engineering topological superconductivity through the synergy of real and imaginary bond modulations, with quantized thermal Hall conductivity as a clear experimental fingerprint.

title: Machine learning based prediction of optical properties in two-dimensional Mo-W-S-Se-Te transition-metal dichalcogenide alloys through physics-informed sampling
summary: Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) alloys provide a compositionally tunable platform for controlling the optical and electronic properties. However, systematic prediction of their dielectric response across multicomponent alloy spaces remains challenging owing to the combinatorial cost of first-principles calculations. In this work, we combined ab initio optical-property calculations with a tabular foundation-model regression to predict the real and imaginary components of the frequency-dependent dielectric function for Mo-W-S-Se-Te TMD alloys. A dataset of 99 alloy structures spanning binary, ternary, quaternary, and quinary compositions was generated using density functional theory (DFT). The resulting polarization-dependent dielectric spectra were used to train a tabular prior-fitted network (TabPFN) and evaluated against the conventional Extra Trees and XGBoost models. To accommodate the in-context capacity limit of TabPFN, we introduced a non-uniform, physics-informed energy subsampling strategy that concentrates sampling in the optically active region above the band gap, where interband absorption is strongest. Trained solely on quaternary alloys, our TabPFN reconstructed the dielectric spectra of held-out quaternary compositions with an R2 > 0.98 and a mean absolute error below 0.10 for all four dielectric components, outperforming both baselines while requiring no gradient-based training or hyperparameter tuning. Our model further predicted derived optical quantities, including refractive index, extinction coefficient, and absorption coefficient. Additionally, our model generalized in a zero-shot manner to binary, ternary, and quinary alloys absent from the training set, with quinary predictions achieving an R2 > 0.97.

AI.tldr: The paper combines DFT calculations with a TabPFN regression model to predict the frequency-dependent dielectric function of Mo-W-S-Se-Te TMD alloys across binary to quinary compositions, achieving high accuracy (R² > 0.97–0.98) with zero-shot generalization and without gradient-based training.
AI.motivation: Systematic prediction of dielectric response across multicomponent TMD alloy spaces is challenging due to the combinatorial cost of first-principles calculations.
AI.method: Ab initio DFT calculations generated 99 alloy structures; a TabPFN model with physics-informed energy subsampling was trained on quaternary alloys and evaluated against Extra Trees and XGBoost.
AI.result: TabPFN achieved R² > 0.98 and MAE < 0.10 for held-out quaternary compositions, outperformed baselines, and generalized zero-shot to binary/ternary/quinary alloys (R² > 0.97).
AI.conclusion: The approach enables accurate, efficient prediction of dielectric properties across broad compositional spaces without hyperparameter tuning or gradient-based training.

title: Exceptional Points in a Parallel Double-Quantum-Dot Josephson Junction Coupled to a Ferromagnetic Reservoir
summary: We investigate exceptional points (EPs) in a parallel double-quantum-dot Josephson junction coupled to a dissipative reservoir. By integrating out the leads, we obtain a non-Hermitian Bogoliubov-de Gennes description wherein the superconducting phase difference and orbital flux govern the complex Andreev spectrum. For spin-independent dissipation, the second-order EPs identified within the infinite superconducting gap limit are eliminated when the finite superconducting gap is properly incorporated. In contrast, spin-dependent dissipation originating from a ferromagnetic reservoir, in conjunction with magnetic flux, gives rise to second-order EPs that persist in superconducting leads with finite gap. Moreover, flux tuning enables the coalescence of two second-order EPs into a third-order EP, whose eigenvalue splitting exhibits cubic-root scaling behavior. A many-body parity analysis establishes the connection between the contrasting finite-gap behavior and the spectral relationship between the even- and odd-parity sectors. Finally, Josephson currents calculated from both the free-energy derivative and the surrogate-model density matrix demonstrate consistency and remain continuous across the EPs. These findings establish spin-selective dissipation and interferometric flux as effective control parameters for robust non-Hermitian singularities in superconducting nanostructures.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates exceptional points (EPs) in a parallel double-quantum-dot Josephson junction coupled to a dissipative reservoir. It shows that while spin-independent dissipation fails to produce robust EPs in finite-gap superconducting leads, spin-dependent dissipation from a ferromagnetic reservoir combined with magnetic flux yields persistent second-order EPs and enables coalescence into a third-order EP with cubic-root eigenvalue splitting. Josephson currents remain continuous across EPs.
AI.motivation: To understand how non-Hermitian singularities, specifically exceptional points (EPs), arise and persist in superconducting nanostructures under realistic finite-gap conditions, and to establish spin-selective dissipation and magnetic flux as controllable parameters for robust EPs.
AI.method: A non-Hermitian Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) description is derived by integrating out the leads for a parallel double-quantum-dot Josephson junction coupled to a dissipative reservoir. The complex Andreev spectrum is analyzed for both spin-independent (normal reservoir) and spin-dependent (ferromagnetic reservoir) dissipation. Finite superconducting gap effects are incorporated, and many-body parity analysis is performed. Josephson currents are computed via both free-energy derivative and surrogate-model density matrix approaches.
AI.result: Spin-independent dissipation yields second-order EPs only in the infinite gap limit, which vanish under finite-gap conditions. Spin-dependent dissipation from a ferromagnetic reservoir combined with magnetic flux produces robust second-order EPs even with finite superconducting gap. Flux tuning allows merging two second-order EPs into a third-order EP with cubic-root eigenvalue splitting. Josephson currents remain continuous across all EPs.
AI.conclusion: Spin-selective dissipation and interferometric flux serve as effective control parameters for robust non-Hermitian singularities (EPs) in superconducting nanostructures, with potential for exploring higher-order EP physics in realistic devices.

title: Ferromagnetic transition in a chiral spin chain
summary: We study the zero-temperature properties of a spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg chain with an additional three-site chiral term of strength $g$. The model is known to be integrable and previous work using Bethe ansatz has identified a phase transition from the usual critical state for $g< g_c = 2/π$ to a chiral phase for $g>g_c$. Here we combine analytical and computational approaches to demonstrate that the transition point comprises an unusual Lifshitz transition with dynamical critical exponent $z=3$, and the chiral phase is a partially spin-polarized phase which spontaneously breaks SU(2) symmetry. We derive a strongly interacting chiral boson field theory for the critical point, and show that even its small-momentum, low-energy response is non-trivial. We also determine the universal properties of the chiral phase, and specifically show that it has a simultaneous quadratically dispersing ferromagnetic "magnon" mode coexisting with the power-law singularities and linearly dispersing excitations typical of a Luttinger liquid. Our conclusions are validated using numerics based on matrix product state methods and exact diagonalization.

AI.tldr: A spin-1/2 Heisenberg chain with a three-site chiral term exhibits a Lifshitz transition at $g_c=2/\pi$ with dynamical exponent $z=3$, and a chiral phase that spontaneously breaks SU(2) symmetry, featuring both a ferromagnetic magnon mode and Luttinger liquid excitations.
AI.motivation: To characterize the zero-temperature phase diagram and critical properties of an integrable spin-1/2 Heisenberg chain with a chiral three-site interaction, where previous Bethe ansatz work identified a critical-to-chiral phase transition but left its nature and the properties of the chiral phase unexplored.
AI.method: Combined analytical (chiral boson field theory, Bethe ansatz) and computational (matrix product state methods, exact diagonalization) approaches to study the quantum phase transition and chiral phase.
AI.result: The transition at $g_c=2/\pi$ is a Lifshitz transition with dynamical critical exponent $z=3$. The chiral phase spontaneously breaks SU(2) symmetry and hosts a quadratically dispersing ferromagnetic magnon mode coexisting with power-law singularities and linear Luttinger liquid excitations.
AI.conclusion: The chiral phase is a partially spin-polarized state with mixed ferromagnetic and Luttinger liquid characteristics, establishing an exotic coexistence of ordered and critical degrees of freedom in a 1D spin system.

title: Determination of fundamental properties of nitrogen from first principles. II. Interaction potential and spectroscopic properties of N$_2$
summary: This work is the second part of the series devoted to first-principles determination of the fundamental properties of nitrogen. In this part, we calculate the potential energy curve for the electronic ground state of N$_2$. The potential is divided into three components: short-, medium-, and long-range, and a different computational protocol is applied to each component, based on a composite coupled cluster approach, genuine multireference methods, and asymptotic expansion of the interaction energy. A particular focus is on the short-range part, as the accuracy of this component is critical from the point of view of metrological applications, including the temperature dependence of many properties of nitrogen gas. Uncertainties of the theoretical data, originating both from basis set incompleteness and applied theoretical method, are rigorously analyzed. The developed potential energy curve is used to calculate the spectroscopic parameters of the N$_2$ ground state and the results are compared with the available theoretical and experimental data.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a first-principles calculation of the N₂ ground-state potential energy curve using a composite approach (coupled cluster, multireference methods, asymptotic expansions) with rigorous uncertainty analysis, focusing on the short-range component for metrological applications.
AI.motivation: To achieve high-accuracy first-principles determination of N₂ fundamental properties, particularly the potential energy curve of its electronic ground state, which is critical for metrological applications such as temperature-dependent properties of nitrogen gas.
AI.method: The potential curve is divided into short-, medium-, and long-range components. A composite coupled cluster approach is used for short- and medium-range, genuine multireference methods for medium-range, and asymptotic expansion for long-range interactions. Uncertainties from basis set incompleteness and theoretical method are rigorously analyzed.
AI.result: Spectroscopic parameters of the N₂ ground state were calculated from the developed potential and compared with available theoretical and experimental data.
AI.conclusion: The short-range component accuracy is critical for metrological applications; the composite approach with rigorous uncertainty quantification yields reliable spectroscopic parameters consistent with experimental data.

title: Cycle-Consistent and Uncertainty-Aware Neural Surrogates for Tokamak Edge Plasmas
summary: The boundary and divertor plasma govern how a tokamak exhausts power and particles, setting heat fluxes, target conditions, and the onset of detachment. Predicting these quantities is essential for operating current and future devices, but edge simulations that resolve them are too slow for parameter scans, optimization, or real-time control. Machine-learning surrogates offer a fast alternative, yet most are forward-only: they cannot recover input parameters from observations or assess the reliability of their predictions. We introduce a cycle-consistent neural surrogate for edge plasmas, combining a conditional U-Net forward model with an optimization-based inverse method built on the frozen forward network. The forward model maps five control parameters to two-dimensional plasma-state fields on the SOLPS-ITER mesh; the inverse method enforces consistency between forward and inverse predictions, a self-supervised quality check needing no ground-truth labels at inference. An ensemble of multilayer perceptrons also predicts electron temperature and density profiles at the outboard midplane and divertor targets, with uncertainty estimates that flag where more simulations are needed. The forward model achieves normalized root-mean-square errors below 2.6% and Pearson correlations above 0.95 for all fields. Cycle-consistency regularization raises the average cyclical $R^2$ from 0.59 to 0.99 without degrading forward accuracy and enables recovery of the core fueling rate; all five control parameters are recovered with Pearson $r\ge0.97$. A $k$-d tree warm start yields a database completion rate above 95%, versus roughly 30% outright failures when cold-started. With about $4\times10^6$ parameters, the model produces full 2D predictions in milliseconds, five to six orders of magnitude faster than SOLPS-ITER, enabling real-time control, parameter scans, uncertainty analysis, and digital twins.

AI.tldr: A cycle-consistent neural surrogate for tokamak edge plasmas combines a conditional U-Net forward model with an optimization-based inverse method, achieving millisecond-scale 2D predictions (vs. hours for SOLPS-ITER), high accuracy (NRMSE <2.6%, R>0.95), and robust recovery of all five control parameters (Pearson r≥0.97) with self-supervised quality checks.
AI.motivation: Edge plasma simulations (SOLPS-ITER) are essential for tokamak power/particle exhaust predictions but are too slow for parameter scans, optimization, or real-time control; existing machine-learning surrogates are forward-only and cannot recover input parameters from observations or assess prediction reliability.
AI.method: A conditional U-Net forward model maps five control parameters to 2D plasma-state fields on the SOLPS-ITER mesh; an optimization-based inverse method leverages the frozen forward network with cycle-consistency regularization; ensemble MLPs predict 1D profiles with uncertainty estimates; a k-d tree warm start initializes the inverse method.
AI.result: Forward model achieves NRMSE <2.6% and Pearson R>0.95 for all fields; cycle-consistency raises cyclical R² from 0.59 to 0.99; all five control parameters recovered with Pearson r≥0.97; database completion rate >95% with warm start vs. ~30% cold-start failures; predictions in milliseconds (5-6 orders of magnitude faster than SOLPS-ITER).
